qt: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

Recent reports have brought to light serious indications of the possible misuse of European funds earmarked for rebuilding Northern Evia following the devastating fires of 20211. Instead of boosting local entrepreneurship, at least 21 investment plans were reportedly approved for the purchase of pleasure boats. The Region of Central Greece reports that audits have so far led to financial corrections of around EUR 2 million and that the findings of an independent audit have been forwarded to the competent public prosecutor’s office. However, these reports raise serious questions about the adequacy of assessment and control mechanisms, the protection of the financial interests of the European Union and, most importantly, the effectiveness of the use of the funds intended for those genuinely affected and for rebuilding the local economy. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of these allegations and the findings of the audits relating to the management of EU funding in Northern Evia?
What measures does it intend to take to ensure that cases are fully investigated and that unduly paid European funds are recovered?

How will it ensure that the funds recovered or released are actually used for the benefit of the residents affected by the fires, local businesses and production activities in Northern Evia, so that the real beneficiaries are not once again disadvantaged by the potential mismanagement of aid?
